Why we built this

A small manifesto for the open web

We made this site by hand — no builder, no framework, just HTML, CSS, and a little JavaScript — as a way of saying thank you. Here's what we believe, plainly.

We believe the internet is at its best when ordinary people can publish without permission, own what they make, and never worry that the ground will shift beneath them.

For more than twenty years, WordPress has quietly made that possible for hundreds of millions of sites. It began in 2003 as a humble blogging tool and grew, in the open, into the software that now powers a remarkable share of the entire web. It did this not by cornering a market, but by giving its power away — under a license that guarantees anyone can use it, study it, change it, and share it.

We love it because it's free

Free as in price: the software costs nothing. And free as in freedom: the GPL license means WordPress can never be taken away, locked down, or sold out from under the people who depend on it. That's not a marketing promise — it's written into the code's DNA. When you build on WordPress, you're building on bedrock that belongs to everyone.

We love it because it's yours

Your words live in your database, on a host you choose, under a domain you own. You can export everything and move it anywhere in an afternoon. No algorithm decides who sees your work; no terms-of-service update can erase it. In an age of walled gardens and rented audiences, that kind of ownership feels almost radical. It shouldn't. It should be normal — and on WordPress, it is.

We love it because of the people

Behind WordPress is one of the largest, kindest open-source communities on Earth. Volunteers translate it into dozens of languages, write documentation, host meetups, and gather at WordCamps in cities all over the world. Companies pledge time through programs like Five for the Future to keep the project healthy for everyone. It is, genuinely, a party — and everyone's invited.

We love it because it keeps getting better

The block editor reimagined publishing as a joyful, visual craft. Block themes and theme.json brought a real design system to the masses. Full-site editing handed the whole canvas to creators. And now, in the AI era, WordPress's open, structured foundation makes it one of the best places to put intelligent tools to work — without surrendering an ounce of ownership.

So this is our love letter. Not nostalgia — gratitude, and genuine excitement for what's next. If you've never tried it, or if you left and have been wondering, consider this your warm invitation back. The block party is still going, and there's a seat for you.

What we stand for

Four beliefs, no fine print

Ownership over rental

Your audience and your archive should belong to you, not to a platform that can change the rules overnight.

Open over closed

Software that anyone can read, fork, and improve is more trustworthy — and more durable — than any black box.

Community over silos

The best tools are made in the open, by many hands, for the common good — and they invite everyone to contribute.

Longevity over hype

We value tools that will still be here, still working, still yours, long after the latest trend has come and gone.

A short history

Two decades of the open web

'03

It begins

WordPress launches as a fork of a small blogging tool — built in the open, licensed under the GPL from day one.

'08

Themes & plugins flourish

A vast ecosystem grows up around the core: a directory of free plugins and themes that anyone can use or extend.

'18

Gutenberg arrives

The block editor reinvents publishing — everything becomes a block, and the canvas opens up for everyone.

'22

Full-site editing & theme.json

Block themes bring a real, visual design system to the whole site — header to footer, no code required.

'26

The AI era

Open APIs, blocks, and MCP make WordPress a natural home for AI-assisted creation — without giving up ownership.

Colophon

How this site was made

Fittingly for a love letter to the open web, every page here is hand-built. No build step, no framework, no tracking. Just files you could open in any browser, read in any text editor, and host anywhere.

  • Vanilla HTML, CSS & JavaScript. Nothing to compile, nothing to install.
  • Type: Fraunces & Inter. Served from Google Fonts; everything else is inline SVG and CSS.
  • Accessible by design. Semantic markup, keyboard support, ARIA, and prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Light & dark, your choice. A theme toggle that remembers and respects your system preference.

Take the pledge

Promise yourself one small thing: your next site will be one you truly own. Drop your email and we'll send you a friendly starter checklist. (This is a demo form — nothing is actually sent.)

Five for the Future

WordPress thrives because people give a little back. Contribute code, docs, translations, or just kindness at a local WordCamp. The open web is built by all of us.
